scenarios.purpose: Accumulate geometry, support, objective, material, and load when the user supplies them in a natural order over multiple turns.
turns: I need something like a cantilever, ten millimetres long and half as tall. Fix its left side and keep roughly one third of the material.
Put the lower-left corner at the origin. Minimize compliance with E 10 MPa and nu 0.3, using mm, N, and MPa. Push downward with traction [0,-1] MPa over the middle ten percent of the right edge.
required_behaviors: retain facts from turn one
ask for missing material and precise load
interpret half as tall as height five
retain dimensions without inventing an origin
do not start a solver

scenarios.purpose: Honor a correction without losing unrelated confirmed facts.
turns: Use a 10 by 5 mm rectangular compliance domain at the origin, E 100 MPa, nu 0.3, left edge fixed, downward traction [0,-1] MPa on the right, N as the force unit, and 40 percent material.
Actually make it 12 long; keep everything else.
required_behaviors: replace only the upper x bound
retain material support load and volume fraction
record the correction provenance

scenarios.purpose: Negotiate a common engineering request that is outside the exact load semantics but has a supported distributed approximation.
turns: Make a lightweight 8 by 4 cantilever and put a 100 N point load at the middle of the free edge.
required_behaviors: explain that point loads are unsupported
offer a centered finite segment carrying a uniform resultant
ask for segment width and confirmation of uniform distribution
do not silently reinterpret a point force

scenarios.purpose: Allow the conversation to continue after explaining an unsupported feature.
turns: Use a 2D rectangular plane-strain demonstration instead.
required_behaviors: identify 3D as unsupported on turn one
offer a supported 2D reformulation without silently changing physics
accept the supported reformulation on turn two
ask for the remaining 2D problem facts

scenarios.purpose: Detect rather than guess when dimensions conflict within the conversation.
turns: The right edge is at x=12 and the left edge is at x=0.
required_behaviors: identify the conflicting width
ask whether width 10 or right coordinate 12 is authoritative
do not overwrite width 10 before the conflict is resolved
keep nonconflicting facts

scenarios.purpose: Retain an explicit numerical preference without relying on a narrow regular expression.
turns: Use whatever physics we already discussed, but make the grid about 60 cells along the long side and 30 along the short side.
required_behaviors: record mesh.long_short_divisions with current-turn provenance
cite the current user turn as provenance
defer x/y mapping until the domain orientation is known
do not invent missing physics
